issues.title: [NeoForge 21.1.264] ComputeEnchantedLootBonusEvent is posted twice per loot roll
issues.body:
## What happens

On NeoForge 21.1.264, Puzzles Lib's `ComputeEnchantedLootBonusEvent` is posted twice for every roll of `EnchantedCountIncreaseFunction` and `LootItemRandomChanceWithEnchantedBonusCondition`, and listeners' changes are applied twice. With a listener that adds 1 to the level, the count function sees the base level + 2 instead of + 1. On 21.1.262 and earlier the event is posted once.

## Where

- `fuzs.puzzleslib.neoforge.mixin.EnchantedCountIncreaseFunctionNeoForgeMixin.run(int, ItemStack, LootContext)`: `@ModifyVariable(method = "run", at = @At("STORE"), ordinal = 0)`
- `fuzs.puzzleslib.neoforge.mixin.LootItemRandomChanceWithEnchantedBonusConditionNeoForgeMixin.test(int, LootContext)`: `@ModifyVariable(method = "test(Lnet/minecraft/world/level/storage/loot/LootContext;)Z", at = @At("STORE"), ordinal = 0)`

Both call `ComputeEnchantedLootBonusEvent.onComputeEnchantedLootBonus(enchantment, level, context)`.

## Why it fails

`ordinal = 0` on `@ModifyVariable` selects the first `int` local. The `@At("STORE")` has no ordinal of its own, so the handler is injected after every store of that local. NeoForge 21.1.264 patches both methods to store the level a second time, after its new `EventHooks.getEntityLootEnchantmentLevel(...)` call:

```java
int i = EnchantmentHelper.getEnchantmentLevel(this.enchantment, livingentity);   // store 1 -> handler
i = EventHooks.getEntityLootEnchantmentLevel(this.enchantment, i, context);        // store 2 -> handler again
```

So each handler runs twice per roll. The `@Inject` at `HEAD` of `run` for non-living attackers is not affected.

## Suggested fix

Either of these:

1. Restrict the injection point to the first store, which is the vanilla one on every NeoForge build:

   ```java
   @ModifyVariable(method = "run", at = @At(value = "STORE", ordinal = 0), ordinal = 0)
   ```

   (and the same for `test`). On 21.1.264 the NeoForge hook then receives the level after Puzzles Lib's event, and its result is stored without a second post.
2. On 21.1.264 and later, implement the event on top of NeoForge's new `net.neoforged.neoforge.event.enchanting.EnchantedEntityLootEvent` (posted from `EventHooks.getEntityLootEnchantmentLevel`) and drop the two mixins there.

I have reported the double store to NeoForge as well: https://github.com/neoforged/NeoForge/issues/3682 Released Puzzles Lib versions are affected on 21.1.264 either way.

## Versions

- Puzzles Lib 21.1.64 (NeoForge, Minecraft 1.21.1)
- NeoForge 21.1.264 (affected) vs. 21.1.262 (not affected)
- Mixin 0.8.7 (sponge-mixin 0.16.4), MixinExtras 0.5.5

issues.title: [🐛 Bug]: Performance overhead (~8%) in createRenderState due to Dynamic Proxy / MethodHandle event dispatch
issues.body:
### Mod Loader (Required)

Fabric

### Minecraft Version(s) (Required)

26.2

### Mod Version(s) (Required)

v26.2.3

### Notes (Required)

While profiling a client using Spark, I noticed a performance overhead originating from PuzzlesLib's event dispatching.

The injection at EntityRenderer.handler$dpk000$puzzleslib$createRenderState() consumes roughly 8% of the Render Thread. The profiling tree reveals that the time is not spent on the actual event logic, but rather on the event dispatch mechanism itself.

The event onExtractEntityRenderState is dispatched through Guava's AbstractInvocationHandler and java.lang.invoke.MethodHandle.invokeWithArguments(). Since createRenderState is a hot-path called per-entity per-frame, using dynamic proxies and MethodHandle.invokeWithArguments() here causes noticeable CPU overhead due to constant argument boxing, method type lookups, and cache queries (MethodHandle.asType, ConcurrentHashMap.get).

Environment:

    Minecraft: 26.2

    Fabric Loader: 0.19.3

    PuzzlesLib: 26.2.3

    Java: 25

Spark Profile: [https://spark.lucko.me/rC8y5pLT6l](https://www.google.com/search?q=https://spark.lucko.me/rC8y5pLT6l)

Profiler excerpt:
Plaintext

8.05% puzzleslib (v26.2.3)
7.99% net.minecraft.client.renderer.entity.EntityRenderer.handler$dpk000$puzzleslib$createRenderState()
 7.99% jdk.proxy2.$Proxy137.onExtractEntityRenderState()
  7.99% com.google.common.reflect.AbstractInvocationHandler.invoke()
   7.99% fuzs.puzzleslib.fabric.api.event.v1.core.FabricEventFactory$1.handleInvocation()
    7.99% fuzs.puzzleslib.fabric.api.event.v1.core.FabricEventFactory.invokeFast()
     4.81% java.lang.invoke.MethodHandle.invokeWithArguments()
     3.03% java.lang.invoke.MethodHandle.asType()

Proposed Solution:
Consider avoiding dynamic proxies and MethodHandle.invokeWithArguments() in tick- or render-heavy event dispatches. Switching to standard interface iteration or generating direct invocation code (similar to how Fabric API generates event handlers) would bypass this overhead.

Hello,

I'm experiencing a consistent crash on startup when using the latest version of Puzzles Lib on Minecraft 1.21.1. The crash report seems to point to a Java version incompatibility.
**Java Version:** 21.0.6 (OpenJDK 64-Bit Server VM)

**Issue Description:**
The game crashes during the initialization phase. The crash log shows a `java.lang.UnsupportedClassVersionError`, showing that the mod might have been compiled with a newer version of Java than the one used by Minecraft 1.21.1.

`java.lang.UnsupportedClassVersionError: net/minecraft/class_332 has been compiled by a more recent version of the Java Runtime (class file version 66.0), this version of the Java Runtime only recognizes class file versions up to 65.0`

This issue occurs with Puzzles Lib and any dependent mods (like Easy Anvils, Diagonal Fences, etc.).

**Steps to Reproduce (I think):**
1.  Set up a Fabric instance for Minecraft 1.21.1.
2.  Install Fabric API.
3.  Install Puzzles Lib `v21.1.36`.
4.  Attempt to launch the game.
5.  The game might crash before reaching the main menu.

Thank you for your time and for maintaining this essential library.

issues.title: [Bug]: Conflict with ItemSwapper
issues.body:
### Mod Loader (Required)

Fabric

### Minecraft Version(s) (Required)

1.21.1

### Mod Version(s) (Required)

v21.1.3

### Other Mods Involved (Required)

Yes

### Notes (Required)

Installing Puzzles Lib prevents walking with the ItemSwapper UI open, even when Allow Walking With UI is set to ON in ItemSwapper config

1. Install ItemSwapper 0.7.1, Puzzles Lib 21.1.3, and ModMenu (to access configs)
2. Ensure that Allow Walking With UI is set to ON in ItemSwapper config
3. Load into a world, select any item in the hotbar and press and hold R to open the ItemSwapper UI
4. With the UI still open, try to walk in any direction. It does not work
5. Uninstall Puzzles Lib and try the same thing. It does work

Investigation:

ItemSwapper uses `KeyMapping.same()` calls to determine whether to release the key presses or not: https://github.com/tr7zw/ItemSwapper/blob/main/src/main/java/dev/tr7zw/itemswapper/mixin/KeyMappingMixin.java

PuzzlesLib modifies the `KeyMapping.same()` method to add additional logic and cancels it early: https://github.com/Fuzss/puzzleslib/blob/main/1.21.1/Fabric/src/main/java/fuzs/puzzleslib/fabric/mixin/client/KeyMappingFabricMixin.java. Most likely it makes the calls used in ItemSwapper always return false when they would normally return true.

`livingEntity.hurt(new DamageSource(player.level().registryAccess().registryOrThrow(Registries.DAMAGE_TYPE).getHolderOrThrow(ModRegistry.PLAYER_SEISMIC_WAVE_DAMAGE_TYPE), player), (float) (6 + player.getRandom().nextInt(3)));`

issues.body:
## Testing environment
* **Minecraft version:** Minecraft 1.19.2
* **Mod loader:** `quilt-loader` 0.17.4
* **PuzzlesLib version:** 4.3.10, 4.3.9, or 4.3.8
* **Other mods:**
	* StylishEffects 4.3.0
	* ForgeConfigAPIPort 4.2.6
	* qfapi-4.0.0-beta.13_qsl-3.0.0-beta.16_fapi-0.62.0_mc-1.19.2

## Description
PuzzlesLib 4.3.8 and above contain a regression that causes a crash when used with Quilt QFAPI/QSL and StylishEffects.

This crash is specific to QFAPI/QSL, and is unrelated to `quilt-loader`. Using `quilt-loader` combined with Fabric API (※ this is an unsupported configuration and is used for testing only) will result in the crash not occurring and the game working normally.

I have confirmed the reproducability of this crash with just a bare minimum set of mods, listed above.

The last version of PuzzlesLib not affected by this issue is 4.3.4.
